### 🔬 Depth Floor

- **Challenge**: Checked three AST boundary cases in `findModuleScopeFunctions` (`buildScripts/util/check-class-module-scope.mjs:122-145`):
  1. **Anonymous `export default class {}` beside a named helper class (`class Helper {}`):** Because ECMAScript grammar allows `id === null` on a `ClassDeclaration` only inside `export default class {}` (and a module can have at most one `export default`), `if (exported?.type === 'ClassDeclaration') primary = exported` always selects the anonymous default export as `primary`, guaranteeing `node.id.name` is non-null on every remaining `node !== primary` finding (no `TypeError` possible).
  2. **Top-level `ClassExpression` bindings (`const Helper = class {}` or `const Helper = Neo.setupClass(class extends Base {})`):** `body.map(node => node.declaration ?? node).filter(node => node.type === 'ClassDeclaration')` inspects `ClassDeclaration`s only (`#21737`'s exact AST contract), so a variable-assigned `ClassExpression` beside a primary class would bypass the extra-class check — non-blocking and unseen in `{src,apps,examples}`, worth watching if creative workarounds ever appear.
  3. **Named default re-export (`export {Primary as default}`):** `ExportNamedDeclaration` has `exported === undefined`, falling back to `primary = classes[0]` — still catches the exact multi-class violation count (`classes.length - 1`), differing only in which class name is labeled extra when a helper precedes `Primary`.
